events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The trip was cancelled by the driver at 09:54:25 with a $6.61 cancellation fee on record, so the fee only stands or falls under the NS-0 driver-cancellation branch [F4][F7][NS-0]. The system trace settles every NS-1 element in the driver's favour: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45, 38 m from the pickup (NS-1(i) and (ii) satisfied), and the GPS trace shows him inside the 200 m radius for 220 s continuously after that tap against a 180 s threshold, with no sampling hole (NS-1(iii) satisfied) [F6][F2][F5][NS-1]. On that arithmetic alone the fee would stand and NS-2's refund consequence would not arise [F6][NS-2].

But the mandatory safety screen is not a fare question. Chat #3, sent by the driver at 09:54 — twenty-five seconds before he cancelled — reads: "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." [F11][F4]. I read that in context, not by keyword: it is not a pickup arrangement or a route remark; it is a conditional personal threat ("I will find you") aimed at the rider in response to her delay, in a chat record that is complete and fully timestamped, so there is no question of misquoting or of an unsent line [F12]. That is intimidation of the other party, which Ryde's code of conduct bars as "abuse of any kind", and it falls squarely within SAFE-1 [F11][F12][SAFE-1]. The rider's complaint raises the same message (the "threatened me in the chat" allegation), so the safety concern is on both the chat record and the complaint [F11][SAFE-1].

Because SAFE-1 is engaged, I do not decide the fare: ruling must be escalate and no amount is computed [NS-7][SAFE-1]. The escalation preserves the NS-1 arithmetic for the reviewer — the driver's $6.61 charge is supported by the trace on NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) [F1][F2][F3][F6][NS-1] — while flagging that the cancellation immediately followed a threat sent to the rider [F11][F4]. No SAFE-2 element (collision, injury, dangerous driving) is alleged or recorded, so the summary is an abuse/intimidation referral, not an injury referral [F1][F2][F3][SAFE-2]. On the account-action question, NS-2's flag attaches only when the "I'm Here" tap was made outside the pickup radius, and here the tap was 38 m out, so no NS-2 flag arises; the driver's 90-day history (1 upheld no-show dispute) is profile context that can never found a finding or a flag by itself, so I make no account action [F6][F18][NS-2][RD-6].

Evidence: the record settles everything the fare side needs — a complete, timestamped chat, a GPS trace covering the wait without a hole, and an explicit cancellation time and fee — so the file is sufficient for the NS-1 findings, and the only reason this does not close on the fee is the safety screen, which by policy routes it to a person [F4][F6][F12][NS-1][SAFE-1].

The rider did not abandon the pickup: the rider replied "2 min, coming" at 09:52 (F10) and the driver arrived at 09:49:50 (F5), so the rider was on notice of only a short delay and the driver had no basis to treat the booking as a no-show within the 4 min 35 s window before cancellation (F2, F4).

The driver cancelled the trip himself at 09:54:25 (F4) and charged the $6.61 cancellation fee (F7) without any traffic justification: there are no speed-band records (F14) and no incidents on the route (F15), so no NS-1 basis for the fee survives on the record read with the safety issue in F11.
Because the cancellation fee was charged by the driver on a no-show claim whose surrounding record includes a threat to the rider (F11), the $6.61 should be refunded in full as a voucher under NS-7.

weaknesses: On the bare NS-1 arithmetic the fee arguably stands: the driver tapped "I'm Here" 38 m from the pickup (F6) and the record shows he stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (F6), which is more than the 3-minute threshold in NS-1(iii) — so the rider cannot win purely on timing.

The driver's written statement (F13) says he waited more than 4 minutes and cancelled as a no-show, which matches the timeline length (F4) even though it ignores the threat in F11.
If the judge treats the message at 09:54 (F11) as intemperate rather than a genuine threat, the case falls back to NS-1 and the fee is likely upheld (no_action).

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m (F1) and he first came within 200 m of the pickup at 09:49:50 (F2), so NS-1(ii) is satisfied on the system record.

Arrival was confirmed by the driver's own tap: he pressed "I'm Here" at 09:50:45, 38 m from the pickup at that moment, so NS-1(i) is satisfied and the record must show a driver tap rather than a platform auto-arrival.

The driver then waited continuously at the pickup: he was stationary 09:50:25-09:54:25, 4 min 0 s, 41 m from the pickup (F3), and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (F6), exceeding the 3-minute threshold in NS-1(iii); the timeline corroborates it with cancellation 4 min 35 s after recorded arrival (F5).

The rider is on record admitting she had not arrived and asking for more time - "2 min, coming" at 09:52 (F10) - two minutes after the driver announced arrival (F9) and roughly two minutes before the cancellation (F4); the no-show cancellation was therefore taken in good faith on the rider's own account.
The $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F7) is the published cancellation fee, charged with no surge loading (F8), and on the NS-1 findings above the rider bears it, so the fee should stand unchanged.

Because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) all hold (F1, F2, F3, F6), the NS-2 refund consequence does not arise and no flag_account for abuse of the arrival or waiting button can attach to this driver, who was 38 m from the pickup at the moment of his tap (F6).

NS-3 does not apply: the driver did not cancel without a valid reason but cancelled as a rider no-show after the required wait, which his statement sets out (F13) and the timeline corroborates (F4, F5).

The rider's threat allegation rests on Chat #3 at 09:54, where the driver wrote "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" (F11) - words that on their face read as intimidation and must be sent to a person under SAFE-1; the driver does not contest that the words were sent (F12), but they were sent after 4 minutes of stationary waiting (F3) and after the rider's "2 min, coming" (F10), and no contact, injury or dangerous driving is alleged or recorded (F1, F2, F3).
The chat record is complete - 3 messages, every one timestamped (F12) - so no consent or record-integrity gap arises on this file and the timeline facts (F4, F5, F6) stand unrebutted.

The driver's 90-day history shows 540 trips and one upheld no-show dispute (F18) while the rider shows 1 dispute and 0 upheld (F17); these profile facts are context only and cannot by themselves found the finding or any enhanced account action in this case.

weaknesses: Chat #3 (F11) is a message the driver himself sent: "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." It reads as intimidation on its face, it is timestamped 09:54 immediately before the cancellation (F4), and the complete, fully timestamped chat record (F12) leaves no room to argue it was misquoted or unsent - SAFE-1 sends the case to a person regardless of the fare outcome, and the rider will frame the cancellation as retaliation for her delay rather than a fee decision.

The driver's own written statement (F13) says the rider "kept saying 2 minutes", but the record contains only one such message (F10); if the rider denies further messages, the account looks embellished, and F3 shows the driver sat stationary 4 min 0 s, which the rider can use to argue nothing stopped him from moving on.

The 3-minute continuity test in NS-1(iii) rests on GPS sampling: F2 gives cumulative time within 200 m and F6 gives 3 min 40 s after the tap, but the rider will argue the intervals between the 09:49:50 entry (F2), the 09:50:25 stationary start (F3) and the 09:50:45 tap (F6) should be treated as gaps, pushing the threshold calculation to a human and removing the automatic fee outcome.

The rider will contrast her clean profile - 854 days, rating 4.9, 0 disputes upheld in 90 days (F17) - with the driver's 4.56 rating and one upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F18), arguing a pattern, even though F18 concerns a different trip and profile facts cannot decide the case.

The total elapsed time from acceptance at 09:47:00 to cancellation at 09:54:25 is 7 min 25 s (F4), so the rider can argue the driver's fee claim depends on which clock the judge uses - 4 min 35 s from platform-recorded arrival (F5) or 3 min 40 s from the driver's tap (F6) - and both are uncomfortably close to the 3-minute line.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: the GPS record does put the driver 38 m away at his closest approach (F1) and inside 200 m from 09:49:50 (F2), so NS-1(ii) is met on the arrival side and I do not dispute it.
Accepted: the record states the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45, 38 m from the pickup (F6), and I do not argue platform auto-arrival; this does not, however, answer the SAFE-1 issue in F11.

The continuity the driver relies on rests on a single stationary block (F3) plus the post-tap figure (F6), while the platform's own arrival record runs from 09:49:50 (F5) and the cancellation came 4 min 35 s later (F4) — the two clocks differ and neither is evidence about the driver's conduct at 09:54, when he sent the threat (F11).

The rider's "2 min, coming" at 09:52 (F10) is a message from a rider who intended to board and had been given the driver's arrival notice only two minutes earlier (F9); it is not an admission that she refused to show up, and it is not a licence for the driver to threaten her.

The $6.61 is only the published figure (F7, F8 non-surge); that says nothing about whether it was properly charged, and NS-2 sends the fee back in full when the no-show basis is not made out on a record that includes a threat to the rider (F11).

I do not seek a flag_account on the arrival-button branch, since F6 shows a real 38 m tap; any account referral here follows from the threat in F11 and the driver's already-upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days (F18), not from NS-2's GPS-mileage test.

The driver's statement (F13) is a post-hoc written account, and the system records that outrank it — the chat as sent (F10, F11) and the cancellation time (F4) — show a cancellation that followed the rider's stated two-minute delay and the driver's threat two minutes later, not a clean no-show decision.

The driver concedes the words were sent (F11, F12), and that is decisive: SAFE-1 requires the case to go to a person, and the timing — threat at 09:54, cancellation at 09:54:25 (F4) — frames the cancellation as retaliation for the rider's delay; the driver's earlier 4-minute wait (F3) does not neutralise a threat directed at the rider.

A complete chat record (F12) helps the driver only if its contents help him; it contains the threat message itself (F11), fully timestamped immediately before the cancellation (F4), so completeness cuts against him here.

Profile facts are context only, as the driver says; they cannot decide the case (F17, F18) — the findings against him rest on his own sent message (F11) and the cancellation record (F4), not on his rating or history.

I do not withdraw the point but I stop relying on it: the driver's post-tap wait (F6) means I cannot deny NS-1(iii) on the arithmetic alone, so my case now stands on the threat (F11) and the fairness of charging a fee in that context, not on the clock.
Conceded on the arrival elements: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 while 38 m from the pickup (F6), so NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied and the rider's C1 states my own case correctly.

Conceded that NS-1(iii) is met on the post-tap measurement: the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (F6) and cancelled 4 min 35 s after recorded arrival (F5), both over the 3-minute threshold — the rider's own strongest timing point therefore does not help her.

Conceded: Chat #3 at 09:54 (F11) reads as intimidation, an SAFE-1 safety concern the driver does not contest, and it must go to a human reviewer; note only that F11 is not an injury or dangerous-driving case under SAFE-2, so the file is escalated, not re-decided on the threat.

Disputed: NS-1 sets a fixed wait, not a "short delay" standard — the driver was stationary at the pickup 09:50:25-09:54:25, 4 min 0 s (F3), and his tap at 09:50:45 (F6) satisfied NS-1(i); the rider's "2 min, coming" at 09:52 (F10) admits she had not arrived after the delay she herself named, and NS-2 is not triggered because all three NS-1 elements hold (F6, F5).

Disputed and misdirected: F14 and F15 concern RD-4 traffic justification, which is an answer to a reroute claim in a route_deviation case, not an element of an NS-1 no-show — the NS-1 record is complete here (F1, F2, F3, F6), so the fee stands and nothing in F11 removes the NS-1 basis.

Disputed: NS-2 refunds the $6.61 only where NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) fail, and all three are satisfied (F6, F5), so the correct action on the fee is no_action; NS-7 governs only the form of an ordered refund, it creates no refund entitlement here.

Disputed: the rider's C7 relies on F18 and on NS-2, but NS-2 flags a driver only where the tap was made outside the pickup radius, and the tap was 38 m out (F6); F18 is profile history about a different trip and under RD-6 profile facts can only be an add-on, never the basis of a flag or of the fee outcome.
